intro: きり comes from 切る, "to cut": the line is cut off right there, and nothing more follows. After a number or これ / それ it means "just this many, and that's it". After a past-tense verb it means "did X, and nothing has happened since". In speech it often becomes っきり.

skills.rule: Number or これ / それ / あれ + きり means "only, and no more"; past verb + きり means "since doing that, and nothing after", usually followed by a negative.
skills.explain:
With numbers of people and times, きり stresses that the count stops there: 二人きりで話したい (I want to talk with just the two of us), チャンスは一度きりです (you only get one chance). With これ / それ / あれ it means "this is the last": 会うのはこれきりにしよう (let's make this the last time we meet). In speech it is often っきり: 二人っきり, これっきり. With ordinary nouns, "only" is だけ, not きり: 水だけ飲んだ.

After the た form, Vたきり describes something that happened once and then nothing more: 兄は朝出かけたきり帰ってこない (my brother went out this morning and hasn't come back). The second half is usually negative (帰ってこない, 連絡がない, 会っていない). Vたきりです can also end the sentence: 一度会ったきりです (I've met him only once, and never again).

Do not confuse it with たばかり, which means "have just done".
patterns: [number of people / times] きり  "only, just"
これ / それ / あれ きり  "the last, no more"
[verb た-form] きり、[negative]  "did X and not since"

examples.jp: 二人[ふたり]{きり}で話[はな]したいです。
examples.en: I'd like to talk with just the two of us.

examples.jp: チャンスは一度[いちど]{きり}です。
会[あ]うのはこれ{きり}にしましょう。
examples.en: Let's make this the last time we meet.

examples.jp: 兄[あに]は朝[あさ]出[で]かけた{きり}、まだ帰[かえ]ってこない。
examples.en: My brother went out this morning and still hasn't come back.

examples.jp: 田中[たなか]さんとは去年[きょねん]一度[いちど]会[あ]った{きり}です。
examples.en: I met Tanaka just once last year, and never since.

examples.jp: 彼[かれ]は「すみません」と言[い]った{きり}、黙[だま]ってしまった。
examples.en: He said "sorry" and then said nothing more.

contrast.note: だけ is the everyday "only" for any noun: 水だけ, 日本語だけ. きり is mostly limited to counts and これ / それ / あれ, and adds "that's all there is, nothing more to come". After a verb, だけ means "just do X" (見るだけ), never "since".
Vたばかり means "have just done": 食べたばかり (I've just eaten). Vたきり means "did and nothing since": 朝食べたきり (I ate in the morning and nothing since). Same verb form, opposite focus.
しか needs a negative verb and puts the stress on "not enough": 一度しか会っていない. 一度会ったきりです says the same fact with the image of a line cut off after that one meeting.

mistakes.bad: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べた{ばかり}、何[なに]も食[た]べていない。
mistakes.good: 朝[あさ]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べた{きり}、何[なに]も食[た]べていない。
mistakes.note: "Ate breakfast and nothing since" is たきり. たばかり means you have only just eaten.

mistakes.bad: 今朝[けさ]は水[みず]{きり}飲[の]みました。
mistakes.good: 今朝[けさ]は水[みず]{だけ}飲[の]みました。
mistakes.note: きり goes after counts and これ / それ / あれ. With an ordinary noun, "only" is だけ.

skills.tip: Did something happen once and then stop dead, with nothing since? たきり. A count with "and that's it"? きり.
